title: Identifying recurrent and persistent landslides using satellite imagery and deep learning: A 30-year analysis of the Himalaya
journal: The Science of The Total Environment
datasets: NASA SRTM 30 m Digital Elevation Model

dataset_roles.dataset: NASA SRTM 30 m Digital Elevation Model

idea.research_question: Where do landslides persist or reactivate across decades, and how can multi-source observations reveal their lifecycle?
idea.hypothesis: Optical scars, terrain controls and human-pressure context jointly improve multi-decadal segmentation and distinguish persistent hazard from land-use change.
idea.mechanism: U-Net segmentation, temporal recurrence/persistence metrics and independent inventory validation
idea.expected_contribution: Transfers routine satellite observations into hazard-lifecycle analysis at mountain-range scale.
idea.falsification_condition: Reject if any required role is omitted, background-only, or not operationally used in the same research instance.

anchor_context.extraction_basis: Full-text seed evidence; empirical results are excluded from the task prompt.
